items.title: Gordon Lorraine — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Ralph Berton one night took me, for the first time in my life, to 52nd Street, which was my dream.

ctx.x: Well, another person whom you met that obviously had a great impact in your life was Alfred Lion, who you later married. Can you talk about meeting Alfred, and how you guys came together. Obviously it was the music that brought you together. But talk about meeting Alfred.

Well, I can thank Ralph Berton for that, because he was playing Blue Note records on the air. Nobody else in this whole town ever played them. He played the 10-inch and the 12-inch. I was fascinated by those records alone. I would sometimes come in to New York from New Jersey with a girlfriend, looking around. Ralph Berton one night took me, for the first time in my life, to 52nd Street, which was my dream. But I could not go alone, and Ralph was a wonderful person, and he took me to Jimmy Ryan’s. I remember…
